Hi Samir — great chatting. High level answers below and I attached a short term sheet for pilot approvals. Marissa (cc) can add more on quantization/quality.

Pilot credit structure (recommended):
- 10k "Optimize credits" applied to observed token-unit consumption after our caching and batching heuristics (not the baseline raw token count). This lets you see net savings in the first month without committing.
- If you convert to a paid pilot (3-month pilot commitment), we can convert credits to a 20% committed-use credit buffer and provide priority routing.

Quantization support:
- We support INT8 for both 13B and 70B variants and an experimental 4-bit path for the 13B where we expect ~8–12% perf regression on instruction-heavy prompts. Marissa will share measured deltas for typical chat prompts.

Caching & batching defaults:
- Start with KV TTL = 30s for chat sessions, max batching window = 40 ms. That usually balances p95 latency and throughput.

I've attached the term sheet (Redwood_Optimize_Pilot_Term_Sheet.pdf). If procurement needs a commercial anchor, we can propose a 25% introductory pilot discount and a one-time implementation credit (up to $6k) tied to successful integration.

Would you be available for a quick 30-min call Monday to walk procurement through the term sheet?

Thanks,
Rachel

Samir — quick technical note on quantization and observed tradeoffs so procurement and infra teams have context.

TL;DR: INT8 is safe for most chat workloads; 4-bit gives the best cost delta but needs prompt-level evals.

Details and suggested guardrails:
- INT8 (production path): expect ~1.2–1.6x throughput improvement and minimal quality regression on system/prompt-following tasks (quality delta typically <4% on our eval sets). Good default for OpsWise 13B/70B variants.
- 4-bit (experimental): 2.0–2.8x throughput improvement; more variable on instruction-heavy or long-horizon reasoning. We recommend running a small A/B eval set (20–50 prompts) before wider use.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache reduces token re-eval by up to 40% for repeat or follow-up turns; monitoring for cache-hit distribution is critical — we'll include TTL and hit-rate dashboards in the pilot console.
- Batching: for p95 ~250ms target, keep batching windows short (25–50 ms) and use adaptive batching with the low-latency policy.

I'll upload a short note with measured deltas from our internal finetune/chat evals (attached). Happy to jump on the Monday call to run through numbers.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

If we can align this week we'll route for signature and schedule integration.

Samir

Folks — internal note before we reply to Samir.

Background: OpsWise is a strategic mid-market account with clear expansion potential in payments vertical. They want 30% pilot discount + cancellation protections. Our standard pilot concession is 25% + up to $6k implementation credit.

Recommendation (conservative):
- Offer 28% pilot discount (midpoint), plus $4k implementation credit, and a 45-day cancellation/30-day data deletion SLA.
- To protect unit economics, attach a conditional clause: if OpsWise consumes >150k effective tokens/month during the pilot, we convert to a paid pilot pricing at 15% off list for remainder of term (with credit throttle to avoid abuse).

Rationale: closes the procurement gap while limiting downside and creating a conversion path. If they push to 30% exactly, escalate to revenue leader.

Karthik
VP, Sales Operations
